headline: Revenue keeps growing, but profit trails a tough comp
summary_short: Revenue rose 4.5% y/y to $528.0M, but operating income fell 23.6% y/y to $146.1M as Q1 2025 booked a $69.8M gain on the Vistar Media stake sale versus $12.6M this year; Adjusted EBITDA still grew 7.7% to $226.3M.
summary_long: Net revenues rose 4.5% y/y to $528.0 million, led by a $23.7 million gain in billboard advertising and $1.4 million in logo revenue, offset partly by a $2.5 million transit decline. Operating income fell 23.6% y/y to $146.1 million and net income fell 27.0% to $101.3 million because Q1 2025 included a $69.8 million gain on the Vistar Media stake sale versus $12.6 million this year; interest expense also rose $2.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes that gain, grew 7.7% to $226.3 million, and AFFO grew 8.0% to $177.5 million. The company expects 2026 distributions of at least $6.40 per share after a $1.60 Q1 dividend. Cash fell to $39.3 million as debt rose to fund acquisitions.

drivers.explanation: Steady outdoor-advertising revenue growth was overshadowed by a tough profit comp: Q1 2025 included a large one-time gain on selling Lamar's Vistar Media stake that did not recur at the same scale.
Billboard net revenues rose $23.7M and logo revenues rose $1.4M, partly offset by a $2.5M decline in transit net revenues.
Gain on disposition of assets and investments fell to $12.6M from $69.8M (2025's Vistar Media sale), plus higher D&A, outweighing revenue growth.
This GAAP-basis EBITDA fell mainly on the smaller disposition gain versus Q1 2025; the company's own Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes that gain, rose 7.7% to $226.3M.
Tracks the same disposition-gain comp plus a $2.2M rise in interest expense from the 2025 note placement; effective tax rate was 3.8% under REIT status.
Net income fell 27.0% while diluted share count fell only 1.3% y/y, so per-share profit declined roughly in step with net income.
Cash used in investing activities rose to $79.4M on higher acquisitions and capex, while financing activities used $93.4M mainly for dividends.
$80.0M of revolver draws during the quarter, partly funding $58.6M of acquisitions, account for most of the increase in long-term debt.
Share count fell y/y reflecting 2025's $150.0M / 1,388,091-share buyback program, even though no shares were repurchased under the program in Q1 2026.
